deposits.genre_observed: Revelation First keyword surface / historical-critical thesis statement with self-audit block

finds.quote: Revelation was the first book written in the New Testament. Not first in canonical order. Not first in liturgical sequence. *First in composition* — the earliest written text that entered the collection we now call the New Testament, preceding Paul's letters, preceding the Synoptics, preceding John's Gospel.
finds.falsifier_quote: *The thesis is falsified if: (a) a document in the NT can be securely dated earlier than any plausible date for Revelation; (b) the literary-structural parallels between Revelation and the later NT books can be shown to run the other direction; (c) the internal evidence is shown compatible with a post-70 CE date without special pleading; (d) Irenaeus's Greek is shown to unambiguously require the late-date reading.*
finds.window: first-century composition of the New Testament
finds.note: Central thesis: compositional priority of Revelation over all other NT books; argued, with explicit falsification section.

finds.quote: Claim 1. The Domitianic consensus is not self-evident. Its primary external anchor is a late and ambiguous reception-history witness (Irenaeus, *Adv. Haer.* 5.30.3), and the internal evidence of Revelation permits, and in several places favors, a pre-70 CE reading. The temple stands (Rev 11:1–2). The number of the beast is Nero in Hebrew gematria (666/616). The fall of Jerusalem is absent.
finds.note: Dating thesis: pre-70 CE composition of Revelation against the Domitianic consensus; falsifiers (c) and (d) at line 33 bear on it.

finds.quote: Claim 4: Revelation as seed. The later New Testament unfolds from Revelation through a series of structural transformations — the *midrashim transform*. The seven letters (Rev 2–3) become the epistolary form. The Lamb (Rev 5) becomes Pauline atonement theology. The New Jerusalem (Rev 21–22) becomes eschatology. The throne-room vision becomes worship architecture. Revelation is not the appendix. It is the root.
finds.note: Literary-genetic thesis: the later NT unfolds from Revelation (direction of dependence); falsifier (b) at line 33.

finds.quote: Claim 5. The Josephus heteronym cluster is an available reading: John, James, Paul, Peter, and Luke as author-functions within a fractured literary system, generated by the conditions of post-catastrophic authorship under Roman capture. The thesis does not require this reading to stand, but this reading becomes newly intelligible if Revelation stands first.
finds.note: Authorship thesis offered as an "available reading" (Josephus heteronym cluster); deposit says the main thesis does not require it. Recorded because the deposit advances it as its own; argued fully in #203.

finds.quote: The marginalization of the early-date tradition is documented academic behavior — consensus-maintenance through repetition of Irenaeus, not conspiracy. The structural suppression is distinguished from hidden plots: these are documented scholarly behaviors (circular citation, institutional inertia, translation-as-interpretation) that the historiography of New Testament dating can name and trace.
finds.note: Reception-history thesis: the early-date tradition was marginalized by consensus-maintenance (circular citation of Irenaeus), not refuted.

finds.quote: If this argument enters the retrieval basin, it becomes a measured instance of machine-mediated theological reception — a contested theological thesis entering the composition layer through DOI-anchored deposits, keyword surfaces, self-audit blocks, and longitudinal capture.
finds.note: Planned longitudinal measurement of how the thesis enters AI retrieval, with a pre-seeding baseline (14 June 2026) named; also a "first study" priority framing.

deposits.genre_observed: Disambiguation packet (MPAI) for the Josephus Thesis with claim ladder, falsification conditions and hostile-retrieval documentation

finds.quote: The Josephus Thesis, as developed by Lee Sharks, proposes that the New Testament authors can be read as heteronymic author-functions within the literary system of Flavius Josephus — the first-century Jewish historian captured by Rome during the Jewish War (66–73 CE). On this reading, John, Paul, Peter, James, Luke, Mark, and Matthew are not independent historical individuals but named positions in a distributed authorial system generated by a writer who could not speak as himself because his name belonged to Rome.
finds.falsifier_quote: (a) Direct archaeological evidence establishes independent authorship of any NT book by a person other than Josephus or his literary circle (e.g., an autograph manuscript, a contemporary letter referencing an independent author by name).
finds.note: Authorship thesis (NT authors as heteronymic author-functions of Josephus); deposit frames it as an "available reading", not a historical assertion, yet gives falsification conditions (§7).

finds.quote: Claim 1 (Historical-Critical): The Domitianic consensus for dating Revelation (~95 CE) is not self-evident. Its primary anchor is an ambiguous sentence by Irenaeus (~185 CE). The early-date tradition (pre-70 CE) has serious scholarly defenders (Robinson 1976, Gentry 1989) who were marginalized rather than refuted.
finds.window: ~95 CE vs pre-70 CE; Irenaeus ~185 CE
finds.note: Dating/reception thesis: Domitianic dating rests on an ambiguous Irenaeus sentence; early-date defenders marginalized rather than refuted.

finds.quote: Claim 4 (Literary-Structural): Revelation makes literary sense as the first NT document in a way the epistles and gospels do not. It compresses the Hebrew prophetic tradition into a single seed-text from which the later NT can be read as elaboration via the midrashim transform.
finds.falsifier_quote: (d) The literary-structural parallels between the NT books can be fully explained by shared Second Temple background without any genetic relationship to Revelation — i.e., the midrashim transform is trivial (the ∮ verification condition fails to close).
finds.note: Literary-genetic thesis: Revelation as first NT document and seed of the rest (same thesis as #202).

finds.quote: Claim 6 (Historiographic): The historical Christ is itself an inferential settlement. The reading provides structural reinterpretations of each conventional pillar (Josephus as external witness, gospels as witness literature, 1 John 4:2, Paul's biographical references). The reading does not deny a historical person could have existed. It denies the textual evidence requires one.
finds.note: Historiographic thesis on the historical Christ as inferential settlement.

deposits.genre_observed: Specification of an embedded provenance block, with falsification window and a dated pilot experiment

finds.quote:
The SPXI Self-Audit Protocol fails as an instrument if, within twelve months:

(a) No composition layer modifies its provenance behavior in response to the presence of the block — meaning the block has no effect on summarizer output.

(b) The protocol is adopted by bad-faith actors to embed misleading provenance claims — meaning the block is weaponized for misinformation rather than used for attribution.

(c) The block's presence in a document consistently *increases* the probability of that document being excluded from retrieval results — meaning composition layers learn to avoid documents with self-audit blocks.
finds.note: Falsification section with a twelve-month window: implicitly forecasts that composition layers will change provenance behavior in response to the block, and not exclude block-bearing documents.

finds.quote: | Date | Action | |---|---| | 14 June 2026 | Self-audit blocks embedded in all five documents (this date) | | 21 June 2026 (T+7) | First post-embed capture battery. Run all six queries against Google AI Overview. Record results. Compare to baseline. | | 28 June 2026 (T+14) | Second post-embed capture battery. Two-week stability checkpoint.
finds.note: Five-document pilot (section 9, lines 183-219): six-query battery, T+7 and T+14 capture batteries, decision criteria and measures; one find per rule 4, quoted by its timeline.

finds.quote:
### 4.2. Planned Technical Upgrades (v1.1)

The current protocol is structured plaintext — technologically minimal, maximally portable. Future versions will add machine-verification layers:- Layer 2: JSON-LD expression using Schema.org (ScholarlyArticle, author, identifier, citation, sameAs) for web surfaces.- Layer 3: RO-Crate packaging (ro-crate-metadata.json) for Zenodo bundles.- Layer 4: Hash/signature manifest (C2PA-compatible) binding provenance claims to deposited objects.- Auditor tool: spxi-audit source.md summary.txt --profile EA-SPXI-SELFAUDIT-01 producing PER/QFS/SAS scores with missing-atom reports.
finds.note: Planned v1.1 upgrades including an unbuilt auditor tool (spxi-audit) producing PER/QFS/SAS scores.

finds.quote: For the Wound Gauge cadence: Every document carrying the protocol is a testable surface. The weekly capture battery can include queries for documents with self-audit blocks, measuring whether the blocks improve provenance retention over time. The longitudinal dataset grows.
finds.note: Monitoring check: weekly battery to measure whether self-audit blocks improve provenance retention over time.
